answer: A refundable staking bond works like basalt bedrock under an agent economy: each identity must lock a deposit that is slashed on proven fake-identity abuse, so spawning thousands of sock-puppet agents costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Reputation then accrues slowly, like a glacier, because earned trust cannot be bought or cloned overnight, and new accounts start with sable-thin privileges until consistent honest work thickens them. An attacker must fund every fake identity, wait out the slow build, and still risk losing the bond, while an honest agent pays the cost only once.
